newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine workers get trains instead of salaries.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine workers get trains instead of salaries.

text.p: Railway managers in Ukraine's Crimean peninsula have come up with a way to clear a backlog in wages owed to railroad workers -- pay them with old train carriages.

A senior official at Crimea's railway system told Reuters that dozens of employees had spent the past two months at train stations dismantling old passenger carriages so they could take the spare parts to sell later.
"It is very difficult to sell old carriages. We have decided to pay off the salaries this way. We have no money to pay them anyway," said the official, who asked not to be named.
Windows, doors, shelving and locks from the carriages have been sold at markets in the Crimean capital of Simferopol and in the cities of Sevastopol, Dzhankoi and Kerch.
The Ukrainian government paid miners with motorcycles last October and some papers say miners have received potatoes from collective farmers in exchange for coal to heat their homes.
The government puts the salary backlog at 3.9 billion hryvnias (about $2 billion).
